overview.description: Idiots (better known as Shithead, Palace, or Karma) is a widespread shedding-type card game. The goal is to avoid being the last player with cards, as that person is declared the 'Idiot' (Shithead). It features a unique three-layered hand structure and several 'magic' cards that can reset, skip, or burn the discard pile.

history.origins: Likely originated in Scandinavia in the mid-20th century spread by backpackers and students. It gained popularity globally in the 1970s and 80s.
timeline: 1970s: Becomes a staple in youth hostels and university dorms.
Present: One of the most common social card games played with a standard deck.
history.evolution: The game evolved from simpler 'beat-the-card' games, adding the face-down 'blind' cards to create a high-tension endgame.
history.cultural: Known for having many names, most of which are pejorative towards the loser.

setup.deck: One deck for up to 4 players, two decks for 5+.
setup.dealing:
1. Deal 3 cards face-down to each player (Blind cards).
2. Deal 3 cards face-up on top of them (Table cards).
3. Deal 3 cards to each player's hand.
4. Players can swap hand cards with their face-up Table cards before play begins.

rules.objective: Be the first to get rid of all cards (Hand -> Table -> Blind).
rules.gameplay:
1. Starting: Player with the lowest card (usually 3) begins.
2. Play: You must play a card equal to or HIGHER than the top card of the discard pile.
3. **Picking Up**: If you cannot play, you must pick up the ENTIRE discard pile into your hand.
4. **Magic Cards**: - **2s**: Reset the pile (can be played on any card). - **7s**: Next player must play a card equal to or LOWER than 7. - **8s**: Skip the next player. - **10s**: Burn the pile (it is removed from the game, and you play again). - **Four-of-a-kind**: Playing 4 of the same rank also burns the pile.
keyRules: Follow the legal action constraints defined for Idiots.
Round outcome is resolved by the scoring method: Scoring summary: First player to shed all cards wins.
Winning condition: Be the first to get rid of all cards (Hand -> Table -> Blind).

strategy.basic: Swap high-value cards (Aces, 2s, 10s) to your face-up Table cards. They are your lifeline for the endgame. Avoid picking up a large pile early on.
strategy.intermediate: If you are forced to pick up a pile, try to do it when it contains many cards of the same rank, allowing you to play them all at once later.
strategy.advanced: Card Counting: Keep track of the 2s and 10s. If your opponent is on their blind cards and you know all the 10s are gone, you can block them with a high King or Ace safely.
tips: Save a 10 or 2 for your very last card if possible.
Don't waste a 2 on a low card; use it to get out of a tight spot against an Ace or King.

list.name: Jokers
list.description: Two Jokers are added as special cards that reverse the direction of play and allow up to six players. In some variants a Joker may be played at any time; when played, the waste pile is given to another player (opponent in two-player; chooser in multiplayer).

list.name: Stacking
list.description: When rearranging before play, players may stack cards of the same rank on top of each other on the upcard piles and replenish the hand from stock; this may be done more than once if more cards can be stacked.

list.name: Tens Restricted
list.description: Tens may not be played on face cards; a player who plays a 10 may take another turn immediately.

difficulty.easy: Plays lowest legal card; doesn't swap cards effectively during setup.
difficulty.medium: Conserves magic cards; swaps high cards to table.
difficulty.hard: Expert probability math; counts magic cards and predicts when to pick up small piles to build better sets.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Suits and ranks are as defined in the deck description above; no separate suit or rank set is used for this game.

notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: Idiots is a shedding game with a single discard pile; there is no play-to-capture or fishing tableau.

hero.title: IDIOTS
hero.subtitle: The Multi-Layer Shedding Game
hero.tagline: Shed your cards fast or become the Idiot. Magic cards change everything.

synthesis.shortDescription: A fast-paced shedding game with three card layers (hand, face-up, face-down) and magic cards that control the discard pile flow.

prompts.human: Welcome to Idiots (Shithead/Palace). You have three layers: hand cards, face-up table cards, and face-down blind cards. Play cards higher than the discard top. Can't play Pick up the pile. Magic cards shake it up: 2s reset, 7s reverse the direction, 8s skip, 10s burn. Last person with cards is the Idiot!
prompts.ai: Game: Idiots (Shithead/Palace). 2-6 players, 52-card deck (2 decks for 5+). Setup: 3 blind face-down, 3 table face-up, 3 hand. Swap: Players swap hand/table cards. Play: Must play equal/higher than discard top. Pick up pile if can't play. Magic: 2(reset) 7(reverse) 8(skip) 10(burn) 4-of-a-kind(burn). Win: First to shed all layers.

scoring.description: First player to shed all cards wins. Last player holding cards loses and is declared the Idiot/Shithead.
scoring.winCondition: First player to empty hand, table cards, and blind cards.

overviewNaReasons.originName: Game has no single documented native name; known as Shithead, Palace, Karma in English.
